title: Cosmos 3 Edge: A 4B World Model for Real-Time Robots
hook: NVIDIA shrinks its Cosmos world model down to 4B parameters and real-time speed — bringing robot perception, prediction, and action generation to edge hardware like Jetson Thor.
key_points: 4B-parameter open world model for robotics, sized to run on memory-constrained edge devices instead of a data center.
Two transformer towers share multimodal attention: an autoregressive tower for vision+text reasoning, a diffusion tower for vision/audio/action generation.
Actions are compact geometric vectors (translation, rotation, manipulation state) — one action format across different robot embodiments.
On NVIDIA Jetson Thor: 32 actions per inference at 640x360, running at 15 Hz real-time control.
Ranks #1 among 4B-parameter models on VANTAGE-Bench for vision analytics.
content_html: NVIDIA released Cosmos 3 Edge, a 4-billion-parameter open-source world model built for robotics and vision AI on edge devices — where memory and compute are tight but real-time response isn't optional.
extra_html: The model pairs two transformer towers that share multimodal attention layers: an autoregressive tower handles vision-and-text reasoning, while a diffusion tower handles vision, audio, and action generation, with separate normalization and MLPs per tower. Actions are represented as compact geometric vectors — translation, rotation, and manipulation state — giving the model one action format across different robot embodiments, so it can double as both a visual predictor and a policy generator. On NVIDIA Jetson Thor it generates 32 actions per inference at 640x360 resolution, hitting 15 Hz real-time control, and it ranks #1 among 4B-parameter models on VANTAGE-Bench for vision analytics. Published by Pranjali Joshi and Saeed Babamohamadi on the Hugging Face blog, July 20, 2026.

related.title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
related.hook: One model that reads and generates language, images, video, audio, and actions — NVIDIA's open Cosmos 3 folds VLMs, video generators, and robot policies into a single backbone.

related.title: Cosmos-H-Dreams: A Real-Time Generative Simulator for Surgical Robots
related.hook: Rehearsing robot surgery on real hardware is slow, costly, and bends instruments. NVIDIA distilled its surgical world model into a two-step student that dreams the operating field at ~160 FPS.

related.title: Geometric Action Model: One Backbone for Geometry and Action
related.hook: GAM turns a pretrained 3D-geometry model into a robot's brain - a single backbone that forecasts both future geometry and the actions to get there, beating heavier VLA baselines.

related.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: A World Foundation Model for Embodied Synthesis
related.hook: Instead of training a robot on real footage, generate the footage: a 38B image/video model that beats GPT-Image-2.0 at imagining robot scenes — and nearly doubles a real policy's success rate.

flashcards.prompt: What lets Cosmos 3 Edge act as both a visual predictor and a policy generator?
flashcards.back_html: Two transformer towers sharing multimodal attention layers — an autoregressive tower for vision/text reasoning, and a diffusion tower for vision, audio, and action generation.

flashcards.prompt: Why does Cosmos 3 Edge represent robot actions as geometric vectors (translation, rotation, manipulation state)?

choices.text: To give one unified action format that works across different robot embodiments
To cut the model's total parameter count
To avoid needing a diffusion tower

flashcards.explanation_html: A shared geometric action representation lets the same model drive robots with different bodies and joints, without an embodiment-specific action head for each.

flashcards.prompt: What real-time performance does Cosmos 3 Edge hit on NVIDIA Jetson Thor?
flashcards.back_html: 32 actions per inference at 640x360 resolution, running at 15 Hz — real-time control speed on edge hardware.
